source.title: Revisiting a Pain in the Neck: Semantic Phrase Processing Benchmark for Language Models
source.authors: Yang Liu; Melissa Xiaohui Qin; Hongming Li; Chao Huang

record.tranche_reason: The study measures downstream task scores across three Llama-2 parameter sizes, a different measure and setting from the original pretraining-loss scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the zero-shot Llama-2 size comparisons on semantic-phrase tasks. The paper does not measure held-out pretraining loss, fit power laws, or test extrapolation. Other benchmark scores, human comparisons, and results that vary prompting or category count do not test the listed scaling claims.
record.test_reason: Zero-shot scores of Llama-2-7B/13B/70B-chat on twelve semantic-phrase task columns (Table 3, Fig. 4) bear on V6: does downstream performance rise with scale. This is a new task setting with only three sizes and no fitted curve, so T3 fits better than T2. No loss, compute, allocation or shape results exist for V1–V5 or V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say Llama ability 'increases steadily' with parameters and attribute this to the scaling law (Kaplan et al.). They note no significant size gap on the similarity-based interpretation tasks (IEI, LCI, NCI), which they blame on insensitive metrics. They do not discuss the non-monotonic or flat results on LCE, NCE, VPE, LVE and VIE that their own Table 3 shows.
record.recipe_differences: Uses zero-shot downstream benchmark accuracy across three Llama-2 sizes rather than measuring held-out pretraining loss, fitting loss laws, or testing compute-optimal training allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed size trend varies by semantic-phrase task and metric; several tasks have small or non-monotonic differences.
record.problems: Only three Llama-2 parameter sizes are compared; no fitted predictive curve or extrapolation is reported. Task metrics differ, and the paper gives no uncertainty for the model-size comparisons in Table 3.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Fitting on small runs and extrapolating to larger ones.
Depth, width or architecture at fixed parameter count.
Any fitted predictive relationship, extrapolation, or link between downstream score and pretraining loss. Only three chat-tuned sizes of one family are compared.
Dependence of exponents or allocation on setup or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: All 36 row values match Table 3. The record's per-size rows each carry the state of the three-point trend. The evidence is weak for V6: three chat-tuned (SIFT) sizes from one family, no uncertainty, no fit, and mixed metrics. The authors' 'steady increase' claim holds for only about 3 of 12 task columns. The category-count and shot-count 'scaling' experiments do not vary model scale and do not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Fitting on small runs and predicting loss on much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
The study compares downstream task scores across three model sizes, but does not fit a predictive relationship, test extrapolation, or relate scores to pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices, and bending of loss curves.

relationships.condition: Zero-shot Llama-2-chat on IED, IEE and LCC (accuracy metrics)
relationships.reason: Clear monotonic gains with size: IED 25.6→37.7→47.9, IEE 53.6→57.2→66.0, LCC 13.7→16.0→28.5 (r01–r06, r10–r12).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy increased monotonically with size: IED from 25.6 to 37.7 to 47.9, IEE from 53.6 to 57.2 to 66.0, and LCC from 13.7 to 16.0 to 28.5.

relationships.condition: Zero-shot Llama-2-chat on NCC, LCE, LCI, NCI, VPE and VIE
relationships.reason: Gains are small (NCC, LCI, NCI) or non-monotonic, with 13B beating 70B on LCE and 13B far below 7B on VPE and VIE (r13–r21, r25–r30, r34–r36).
relationships.display_finding: NCC, LCI and NCI gains were small, while 13B exceeded 70B on LCE but fell far below 7B on VPE and VIE.

relationships.condition: Zero-shot Llama-2-chat on IEI, NCE and LVE
relationships.reason: No gain from 7B to 70B: IEI 85.8→86.6 (authors: not significant), NCE 40.5→39.1, LVE 4.4→3.8 (r07–r09, r22–r24, r31–r33).
relationships.display_finding: From 7B to 70B, IEI changed nonsignificantly from 85.8 to 86.6, while NCE declined from 40.5 to 39.1 and LVE from 4.4 to 3.8.
